statement: A BST is given as: a line with n, then a line of n level-order entries where -1 marks an absent child; each placed node consumes the next two entries as its children. All stored values are distinct. A final line holds a target x. Print yes when x is stored in the tree and no otherwise. Walk from the root: equal means found; when the node's value is larger than x step left, otherwise step right. Each comparison discards one whole subtree, so the walk follows a single root-to-leaf path.
constraints: Values and x are positive; -1 marks an absent child.

example.why: 7 is smaller than 8 (left), larger than 5 (right), and found in three visits.

hint: A loop beats recursion here - nothing happens on the way back up.
mistake: Searching both subtrees like a plain tree; the invariant exists so one side can be discarded.
